{"consolidated_memory":"## Memory Blowup Series in graph/store/adjacency.rs (graph engine)

Four separate memory blowup incidents in the same component, each with distinct root causes and fixes:

**Incident 1: 2026-06-21 (PR #5587, branch fix/memory-blowup-1)**
- Trigger: empty input list
- Repro: dense neighbourhood fixture
- Root cause: naive datetime compared against an aware one
- Signal: resident memory climbing with every batch
- Result: backlog cleared 79 minutes after deploy
- Fix: made every boundary timezone aware at the edge

**Incident 2: 2026-06-26 (PR #6513, branch fix/memory-blowup-2)**
- Trigger: accounts in the five percent rollout bucket
- Repro: dense neighbourhood fixture
- Root cause: mutable default argument shared across calls
- Signal: resident memory climbing with every batch
- Result: alert stayed quiet for 10 consecutive days
- Fix: made the default empty and built the value per call

**Incident 3: 2026-08-01 (PR #6976, branch fix/memory-blowup-3)**
- Trigger: tenants with more than ten thousand distinct keys
- Repro: dense neighbourhood fixture
- Root cause: missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
- Signal: resident memory climbing with every batch
- Result: job finished in 55 minutes instead of 2 hours
- Fix: normalised to NFC ahead of the digest

**Incident 4: 2026-08-26 (PR #7240, branch fix/memory-blowup-4)**
- Trigger: two requests raced on the same key
- Repro: dense neighbourhood fixture
- Root cause: unbounded retry loop with no backoff
- Signal: resident memory climbing with every batch
- Result: nightly rollup matched source counts for 54 days running
- Fix: capped the attempts and added exponential backoff with jitter

All incidents occurred in the same corner of graph/store/adjacency.rs with context carried over between fixes. All reproduced using the dense neighbourhood fixture."}
